nodes.name: Impregnation
nodes.procedure: The Ru precursor is uniformly mixed into the suspension of the support material, and then the mixture is dried and calcined to remove the volatile components so that Ru is deposited on the surface of the support. Zhang et al. synthesized a single-atom Ru-supported MoS2 (SA-Ru-MoS2) HER electrocatalyst by a simple one-step impregnation method.

nodes.name: Solvothermal Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: Luo et al. proposed a strategy of lattice-constrained in situ reduction effect with a 3D crystal fullerene network (CFN), mainly limiting Ru species to the lattice of the fullerene network to construct RuNP-RuSA@CFN-800. The assembly of Ru3+ was first synthesized by solvothermal method and then pyrolyzed at 800°C.

nodes.name: Coprecipitation Calcination
nodes.procedure: Sun et al. synthesized a Ru1/FeOx single-atom catalyst for water gas shift (WGS) reaction by coprecipitation method, which can achieve high CO conversion with a low loading of 0.18 wt%. The insoluble metal hydrated oxide or metal salt is precipitated by dropping precipitant into the aqueous solution of the precursor, and then a series of filtration, washing, and calcination is carried out.
